verify_first.label: Resolve this before anything else
verify_first.body: Two logging questions now matter more than any single minimum. (1) The September ATP export left Night and XC blank on three flights that were clearly both: the 9/14 2-hr day XC to KMQY, the 9/15 2-hr night XC, and the 9/29 Duties-of-PIC Night to KCHA (~6.8 hrs). Get those corrected in the school's records — until they are, Night, Cross Country and PIC Cross Country read low. (2) Strict PIC jumped to 123.3/250 (49%), but 16.0 of that is Seminole time the export logs as PIC. Without a multi-engine rating that time isn't loggable PIC under 14 CFR 61.51(e)(1), so the conservative figure is ~107.3/250 (43%). The SIC-combination question from earlier reviews still stands (PIC+qualifying-SIC 424.6/250), but it's no longer the only open item.

stalled.label: Frozen on paper — a records gap, not a flying gap
stalled.body: Night (48.0/100), Cross Country (367.5/500) and PIC Cross Country (51.5/100) haven't moved since the September 1 review, even though September included both commercial 2-hr cross-countries and a night flight to Chattanooga. That's the blank columns in the export, not missing experience. Once the three entries above are fixed, Night should rise to roughly 52–53 and both XC numbers should climb. If they don't, look at the flights again before scheduling extra legs.

resolving_naturally.label: Milestone crossed — Multi-Engine Land is done
resolving_naturally.body: Multi-Engine Land: 29.8/25 (119%) — closed out. The two 9/15 Seminole sessions (6.0 hrs) and 9/29 (2.0 hrs) took it past the line, so it no longer needs watching. Commercial single-engine work is also moving along: maneuvers were introduced 9/14, both required 2-hr cross-countries are logged, and the remaining weak spot in the debriefs is soft-field nose protection, not anything hours-related.

highest_leverage.label: Highest-leverage move for total hours
highest_leverage.body: 594.8/750 (79%), with 155.2 hrs left. 28.6 hrs have been added since the 9/1 review, almost all between 9/13 and 9/29, which works out to about 28 hrs/month, the same as last cycle. At that rate you reach 750 in roughly five and a half months (around mid-March 2027). The CFI phase plus building time as an instructor is what shortens that. No single category is holding up total time.

lagging.label: Lagging without a natural fix
lagging.body: PIC Night: 1.6/25 (6%) — still the one minimum nowhere near done. Fixing the two September night flights in the records could add up to ~4.8 hrs, if the school's PIC logging holds (both were dual), which would bring it to about 6.4. That still leaves ~19 hrs that only come from deliberately scheduled night legs flown as PIC. Night overall (100 needed) shares that fix, so every PIC night hour counts toward both.
